rows.notes: The study is a narrative review of UAS applications in wildlife science plus a systematic bibliometric review of wildlife journals (counting records alluding to aircraft, satellites and tracking devices). It reports no own measurements of wildlife disturbance by UAV flights. Disturbance is discussed only in Section 2.4 by summarising cited studies (Sarda-Palomera 2012, Chabot 2015, Ditmer 2015, Vas 2015, etc.), with the stated general consensus that UAS cause low to no disturbance in overflights but that close-up flights elicit stronger reactions (parents flying away, alarm calls, dive-bombing) and that caution is needed. Nothing on lithium-ion battery disposal. Because it is a review, Q1 is 'no' and all other questions are 'no'; the claim about disturbance is at most partially supported by cited work, not by the study's own data.

notes: Full text appears complete (pp. 137-155). The paper is a review article; its systematic literature search produces bibliometric counts about aerial platform usage in the literature, not primary data on the claimed effect.
